questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best museums to visit in London
The history of dinosaurs and fossils
How big national museums are built
The debate over objects taken by empires
questions.why: Beth says they'll discuss the controversial role of museums, which are criticised for stealing ancient treasures.

questions.q: What surprising fact about London tourists does Neil mention?
options: Most prefer shopping to sightseeing
Many tourists' top destination is a museum
Few tourists visit Big Ben
Most tourists go to fashion shows
questions.why: He asks if it would surprise you that many tourists' top destination is actually a museum.

questions.q: What criticism of museums does Beth mention?
options: They are too expensive for families to visit
They have too few visitors on weekdays
They took treasures during imperial times
They only show British history and art
questions.why: She says many museums are criticised for stealing ancient treasures during imperial times.

questions.q: According to Professor Adam Kuper, what did the imperial ideology believe?
options: Societies progress, and Europe should lead others
All cultures are equal and should be left alone
Hunter-gatherers were the most advanced people
Religion is always better than science
questions.why: He describes the idea of 'onwards and upwards', helping other people 'up the ladder with us'.

questions.q: What did the opposing 19th-century view say?
options: Only European culture should be protected
There are no better or worse cultures
Museums should close
Farming was a mistake
questions.why: It said, 'There are no better or worse cultures, there are just national cultures.'

questions.q: Why does Beth say returning stolen objects is complicated?
options: Because museums don't know where they are
Because the objects are too fragile to move
Because nobody wants them back
Because they're very old and their history is complex
questions.why: She asks to whom centuries-old objects should go, and says their history is complicated.

questions.q: Why does Beth mention the Benin bronzes?
options: To show that local leaders' actions can also be questioned
To show that they have already been returned
To say they are the museum's most popular objects
To explain how bronze is made
questions.why: She says questions can be asked about the actions of local leaders as well as European powers.

questions.q: What kind of exhibitions does Professor Kuper want to see more of?
options: Permanent exhibitions about one tradition
Exhibitions only about European art
Short shows about links between cultures
Exhibitions without any historical objects
questions.why: He wants more temporary exhibitions about the relationships between different cultural traditions.
